The Setting

A “small” hospital, a big responsibility

NTUH Hsinchu Branch — carrying 24-hour primary PCI in a region that once had no medical center
550

Acute beds

≈ 819 total beds; ICU / CCU 49

3,000

Caths / year

Open-heart surgery 200 / year

24 hr

Primary PCI

Year-round emergency reperfusion

2,500

OPD / day

ED 200 · admissions 70 / day

Before 2001 there was no cath lab and no medical center in the Hsinchu district. For STEMI, every minute is myocardium — building a local, round-the-clock primary-PCI network was an urgent need.

04
Time is Muscle

The D2B clock actually starts at the ECG

The treatment target for STEMI is Door-to-Balloon (D2B) < 90 min. But the whole timeline begins with recognising STEMI on the ECG.

If Door-to-ECG (D2E) is delayed and STEMI is not identified early, no cath lab can make up the lost time. D2E (target < 10 min) is the hidden gateway to D2B.

Door → ECG (target)
<10min
the gateway: recognise STEMI
Door → Balloon (target)
<90min
the international reperfusion goal

The Journey · Three Phases

A decade of quality improvement

PHASE 1

Beginning

Build the in-hospital system & team; push D2B target rate from ~40% to 60–70%.

2006–2010 · D2B ≈ 50%
PHASE 2

Restructuring

Reach beyond the hospital walls — fix the transfer-in delay through inter-hospital coordination.

Transfer-in · DIDO
PHASE 3

Re-start

Attack the last mile — the Door-to-ECG bottleneck — and push the target rate above 90%.

2011–2015 · D2B ≈ 75% → 90%+

Each phase had a different bottleneck — “the cause keeps changing” is what makes quality improvement hard.

Easy vs Hard

Some problems yield easily — others don't

Easy to fix

Workflow & technique — solved with flow charts, algorithms and training.

→ D2B rate: 40% → 60–70%

Hard to fix

Diagnostic flow & human behaviour — judgement and habit resist change.

→ D2E rate: 60% → 70% (limited)

Flow and technique moved D2B a lot — but D2E stalled. This foreshadowed the real fight ahead: diagnosis.

Three in-hospital arrows

Restructuring · Beyond the Walls

In-house is fixed — so why is the overall D2B still not good enough?

TRANSFER-IN · INTER-HOSPITAL COORDINATION
The Transfer-in Problem

Transferred patients drag the total D2B

12
Door-in to Door-out

The bottleneck is the referring hospital's stay

13
Solutions · Beyond the Walls

Re-engineer the process outside the hospital

  • Shared inter-hospital duty-staff roster — always reach the right person
  • LINE instant-messenger groups — one-to-all, rapid; activation is no longer confined to the ED
  • Uniform activation window; immediate ECG transfer; Killip class; activate before arrival
  • ED prepared, ICU bed reserved, cardiology & cath team arrive early
  • Perform the ECG in the ambulance to buy time
14
Prehospital

Let the ECG happen on the ambulance

15
ACS Out-reach Program · 2013

Open emergent ECG interpretation to partner hospitals

An emergent ECG-interpretation service: partner ED physicians join by smartphone and get real-time cardiology reads. Online since 2013.

Launched only after resolving the legal / privacy debate — physician-patient relationship, informed consent, data leakage & storage, and physician responsibility were each addressed.

  • Partner ED physician evaluates first, then discusses with cardiology
  • STEMI: direct line to selected partner hospitals
  • Affiliated hospitals: smoother transfer, bed reserved
  • Quality improvement is no longer confined to our own hospital

03

Re-start · The Last Mile

Beyond 75% — is it worth pushing further? Yes, because diagnosis is still unsolved.

2011–2015 · CONQUER DOOR-TO-ECG
Beyond 75% · Does it worth?

Faster systems, and the outcome debate

18
Why Door-to-ECG?

Two forces pointed at the same gate

Driver 1

Accreditation requirement

Hospital accreditation counts “first ECG < 10 min”. ACS here is defined by discharge diagnosis and includes NSTEMI — so missed or late ECGs are penalised.

Driver 2

Reflection from cases

Reviewing missed cases — including those diagnosed only at discharge, and NSTEMI — all pointed back to one gate: the ECG not done or read early enough.

The remaining obstacle is clear — diagnosis. And diagnosis begins with one electrocardiogram.

19
Cause-and-Effect · D2E > 10 min

Why is D2E < 10 min achieved < 75%?

Root-cause (fishbone) analysis — the bottleneck is the time to perform the ECG

Process

  • No priority rule for ECG
  • No rule on when to activate
  • No mandate to perform ECG

People

  • Triage nurses not allowed to do ECG
  • ECG technicians busy / unaware of urgency
  • Not enough staff for urgent ECG

Training

  • Insufficient cross-team discussion
  • Cases not reviewed one-by-one

Environment

  • No reserved space for ECG machine
  • Machine far from triage; congestion
20
Analysis · D2E > 10 min

Diagnosis delay, driven by atypical symptoms

21
Solutions · Fix the ECG Bottleneck

Space, people, protocol, monitoring

Space

ECG at triage

Machine moved to the triage area.

People

Nurse-initiated ECG

Triage nurse performs ECG without a physician order.

Protocol

6-symptom rule

Mandatory ECG for the six red-flag presentations.

Monitor

Audit + reward

Continuous monitoring; reward cases that meet the goal.

Six red-flags → mandatory ECG: chest pain · dyspnea · bradycardia · hypotension · dizziness + hypotension · epigastralgia (age ≥ 40)

22
Protocol · Symptom-triggered ECG

Five red-flag symptoms that trigger an immediate ECG

Any one of these at triage → a 12-lead ECG is performed at once by the triage nurse, without waiting for a physician order
01

Chest pain

Typical or pressure-like chest discomfort

02

Dyspnea

Unexplained shortness of breath

03

Bradycardia

Slow heart rate

04

Hypotension

Low blood pressure

05

Dizziness

Especially with low blood pressure

＋ Special criterion: epigastralgia (upper-abdominal pain) in patients ≥ 40 years. Atypical presentations are the leading cause of missed STEMI — this rule catches them early.

23
Do it right, every time

Standardise, then monitor relentlessly

  • A standardised D2B record sheet captures each time-stamp and every cause of delay
  • Multiple elements monitored regularly — not just the headline number
  • Cases that meet the goal are rewarded; misses feed the next review

“Early ≠ more.” The aim is to move the ECG earlier in the pathway — a change of sequence and rules, not of headcount or spending.

Results · The Evidence

A before-and-after quality-improvement study — the data must be honest.

PLOS ONE, 2019 · e0222019
Study Design

Balanced before / after cohorts

Interventions 2014/6–10 (ECG at triage; nurse-initiated ECG). One year before (N=109) vs one year after (N=105).
26
Primary Result

The target-achievement rate jumped

Door-to-ECG < 10 min
79.8%→93.3%
p = 0.005
Door-to-Balloon < 90 min
76.2%→91.1%
p = 0.007

Notably, the median times barely moved (D2E 4→5 min; D2B 66→65 min). What changed was the target-achievement rate — pulling the tail of late patients inside the threshold.

Recognition

From best-abstract award to peer-reviewed print

35
Publication · PLOS ONE 2019

The paper, at a glance

Lee CK, Meng SW, Lee MH, …, Hsieh MY, Huang YC, Huang EP, Wu CC. The impact of door-to-electrocardiogram time on door-to-balloon time after achieving the guideline-recommended target rate. PLoS One. 2019;14(9):e0222019.
Background

The unknown gate

After D2B-Alliance QI strategies, the components of D2B — and the role of D2E — were poorly defined.

Methods

Before / after

ED interventions Jun–Oct 2014 (protocol-driven ECG; ECG station + technician moved to triage). 214 STEMI: 109 before / 105 after.

Results

D2E is the lever

D2E was the most critical delay (20.8%). D2E<10min 79.8→93.3% (p=.005); D2B<90min 76.2→91.1% (p=.007); benefit only in walk-in patients.

Conclusion

Fix triage, fix D2B

Protocol-driven, multidisciplinary ED triage improves D2E and thus D2B<90 — earlier STEMI recognition in ambiguous presentations.

Adjusted finding: the QI intervention was an independent predictor of meeting the D2E target (OR 3.83, 95% CI 1.32–11.1; p=0.013).

36
Take-home Message

Five lessons

  • No monitor, no improvement. What you don't measure, you can't move.
  • Help yourself vs. help everyone. Quality improvement must reach beyond your own walls.
  • The cause keeps changing. Re-analyse — today's bottleneck is not yesterday's.
  • Knowing ≠ doing it right. Implementation fidelity is everything.
  • Communication · Standardization · Monitoring. The three engines of durable change.
